sections.heading: When a Karns roof is due for replacement

If your roof is in that range and you see curling or cracked shingles, bare spots where granules have washed into the gutters, or more than one leak in a season, it's worth getting a replacement price alongside a repair price.

In the newer subdivisions, the question is often whether the original builder-grade roof was installed and ventilated well. sections.heading: What replacement involves on Karns homes
body: Most replacements here are asphalt shingle tear-offs: the old roof comes off down to the deck, damaged decking is replaced, then underlayment, ice and water membrane in valleys and around chimneys and pipes, new flashing, shingles and ridge ventilation go on. On older homes, it's common to find more than one layer of old shingles or decking that needs repair, so ask each roofer how they'll price that before work starts.

Terrain matters too. Homes up on the slopes of Beaver Ridge and Copper Ridge catch more wind, so ask about the manufacturer's high-wind nailing pattern. Houses on wooded lots near Beaver Creek get more shade, leaves and moss, which makes algae-resistant shingles and good gutters worth considering. Parts of the creek valley are mapped floodplain, so a replacement is a good time to make sure downspouts carry water well away from the foundation.

sections.heading: Licensing and paperwork in Karns

Knox County is one of the Tennessee counties where residential roofing jobs from $3,000 to $24,999 require a state Home Improvement license, and jobs of $25,000 or more need a state contractor's license. Look up any roofer at verify.tn.gov before you sign.

Tennessee also limits home improvement deposits to one-third of the contract price. If your subdivision has a homeowners association, check its rules on shingle color and style before you choose, so your new roof isn't held up by an approval.

sections.heading: What a tear-off can uncover on older Maryville houses

intro: Many Oak Ridge houses have outlived their planned life several times over. sections.heading: What sits beside the roof on a cemesto house
body: When the Oak Ridge Historic District was documented for the National Register in 1991, every cemesto house had already received a newer asphalt-shingle roof, but only about one in five still showed its original cemesto siding. Many owners had covered the panels with aluminum or vinyl, so the walls next to your roof may still be cemesto underneath.

That matters because new step flashing and counterflashing go where the roof meets those walls. Cemesto is a cane-fiber insulating board faced on both sides with asbestos cement, and the EPA lists asbestos cement products among older building materials that may contain asbestos. Ask each roofer how they would flash those walls without cutting or breaking the panels, and whether sampling by an accredited professional is included or priced separately.

sections.heading: Chimneys, additions and wooded ridge lots
body: The nomination describes a central interior chimney on every A-house, an interior end chimney on the C, and a chimney on the raised section of the D-house roof. A replacement is the time to reflash a chimney or take an unused one down below the roofline, and to inspect the seams where later bedroom and living-room additions tie into the original roof.

The nomination notes that the living area almost always faces the back, wooded side of the lot, so extensions there often sit under trees, and some F-houses stand near the top of the ridge on Outer Drive. Quotes should account for tree cover, sloped yards and where a dumpster can sit.

sections.heading: Flat roofs and roofs that used to be flat
body: Several of the concrete-block models in Woodland and Scarboro were built with flat composition roofs over wood sheathing and rafters, and once residents could buy their homes in 1956, adding a gable roof became a common change in Woodland. If yours is still flat, you are pricing a low-slope membrane, which 2026 guides put at about $5.50 to $12 per square foot for TPO and $2.50 to $4.50 for modified bitumen. If it was converted, ask the roofer to check the framing that was built over the old flat roof.

sections.heading: Permits, licensing and a ballpark price
body: Oak Ridge's Codes Enforcement Division, in the Planning and Development Department at 200 South Tulane Avenue, issues the city's building permits and lists the 2024 International Residential Code. It also says it issues building trade permits to applicants holding a valid City of Oak Ridge or State of Tennessee license for the work, so ask who will pull any permit and under which license.

Neither Anderson nor Roane County adopted the state Home Improvement law, so only jobs of $25,000 or more trigger a state contractor's license. Modernize puts a 2,000 square foot architectural-shingle roof in the Knoxville area at about $11,500 to $20,000.

checklist: Ask how wall flashing will be handled where siding covers original cemesto
Confirm whether asbestos sampling is included, excluded or priced separately
Ask whether each chimney will be reflashed, rebuilt above the roof or removed
Have the roofer inspect every seam where an addition meets the original roof
For a flat roof, get the membrane type, insulation and drainage plan in writing
Ask who pulls any city permit and under which license
Plan truck and dumpster access on steep or wooded lots

faqs.q: Does the roof on my cemesto house contain asbestos?
faqs.a: The 1991 National Register nomination lists cemesto as a wall material and asphalt as the roofing, and it found every cemesto house already reroofed. Older layers and siding can still contain asbestos, though, and the EPA lists roofing and siding shingles among products that may. Only sampling by a trained, accredited professional before anything is disturbed can tell you.

faqs.q: Which office handles building questions for a reroof in Oak Ridge?
faqs.a: Inside city limits, the Codes Enforcement Division of the Planning and Development Department issues building permits and enforces the city's construction codes, whichever county your home is in. Its general line is 865-425-3532, and it is at 200 South Tulane Avenue. Ask your roofer to confirm with that office whether your job needs a permit.

faqs.q: Can I put a pitched roof on my flat-roofed Woodland or Scarboro house?
faqs.a: Owners have been doing it since the houses went up for sale in 1956; the National Register nomination for the Woodland-Scarboro district calls it a common alteration in Woodland. It is framing work, not just roofing, so talk to Codes Enforcement before you plan on it. National Register listing alone does not restrict what a private owner does with private funds, according to the National Park Service.

h1: Roof Repair Quotes in Oak Ridge, TN
hero_subtitle: A limb through the shingles, a worn flat roof or failing chimney flashing: request repair quotes from up to 3 licensed, insured roofers who work on Oak Ridge homes. Free to ask, no obligation.
intro: Oak Ridge has an unusual mix of houses to repair: wartime cemesto homes, TVA flat-tops brought in during the war, postwar concrete-block houses and duplexes, ranch houses, and new construction at Rarity Ridge. A repair on one of these often comes down to a single detail, such as a chimney, the seam over an addition or the edge of a flat roof. This page covers the repairs worth knowing about, the trees and storms behind them, and how to keep a repair the size it needs to be.

sections.heading: Trees, ridges and storm damage
body: Oak Ridge's older neighborhoods follow curving streets laid out to fit the ridges, and many lots are wooded right up to the house. Limbs that hang over a roof can crack or puncture shingles in a storm, and leaves that settle in valleys and gutters hold water against the roof edge. After high wind, check the slopes under overhanging trees first.

Hail reaches the area too. On May 16, 2023, the National Weather Service received reports of hail from 0.7 to 1 inch about six miles northeast of Oak Ridge. Stones in that range tend to leave marks on aluminum gutters, vent caps and flashing, which helps a roofer judge whether the shingles took hits as well.

sections.heading: Flat-tops and flat-roofed postwar houses
body: The TVA flat-tops brought to the townsite during the war, models RB-1 and RC-1, were frame houses with plywood walls meant to last six years. In Woodland and Scarboro, several 1949 concrete-block models were built with flat composition roofs over wood sheathing. Repairs on low-slope roofs like these often involve blisters, open seams, worn edge flashing and low spots where water ponds.

Before accepting a quote, ask the roofer to identify the existing membrane, whether modified bitumen, EPDM, TPO or an older built-up roof, and to patch it with compatible material. A patch that doesn't bond to the roof around it can become the next leak.

sections.heading: Chimneys, additions and old siding
body: On A-type cemesto houses the chimney rises through the center of the roof, so its flashing is the first thing to check when a stain appears near the middle of the house. The other weak point is the joint where a postwar addition was tied into the original roof.

If a repair means lifting siding to replace step flashing, keep in mind that the panels underneath may be original cemesto, which is faced with asbestos cement. Ask whether the repair can be done without disturbing them, and if not, whether testing comes first.

sections.heading: Licensing, permits and price for small jobs
body: Anderson and Roane counties are outside Tennessee's Home Improvement license program, so the state license requirement only starts at $25,000, well above a typical repair. For smaller work, TDCI suggests checking with the local codes office about licenses and permits; in Oak Ridge, that is the Codes Enforcement Division on South Tulane Avenue. HomeAdvisor's 2026 national range for a typical repair is about $395 to $1,968.

checklist: Note which trees overhang the damaged area
Ask the roofer to identify your flat roof's membrane before patching
Ask whether repairs near walls will disturb siding or cemesto panels
Confirm whether chimney flashing will be replaced or only resealed
Get photos of the damage and of the finished repair
Get the price and payment terms in writing before work starts

faqs.q: My Oak Ridge flat-top has a spot where water ponds. Is that a repair or a new roof?
faqs.a: It depends on what is under it. If the deck is sound and the membrane is in fair shape elsewhere, a roofer may be able to repair the area or build up the low spot so water drains. If the membrane is cracked or blistered across the roof, or the deck is soft, replacement is usually the better use of money. Ask for both prices.

faqs.q: My house is in the Oak Ridge Historic District. Does that limit repairs?
faqs.a: Not by itself. The National Park Service says National Register listing places no restrictions on what a private owner does with a property using private funds, though state or local rules can still apply. Telling the roofer the house's age and type still helps, since it signals older materials and framing they should expect.

faqs.q: Can one side of a Scarboro or Woodland duplex roof be repaired on its own?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. A repair can be limited to one unit, but on duplexes such as the hipped-roof Model 20, which has two chimneys at the crest, water entering on one side can travel. Let the neighbor know before work starts, agree on ladder access, and ask the roofer to check the shared ridge while they are up there.

h1: Roof Leak Repair in Oak Ridge, TN
hero_subtitle: Drip by the chimney, a stain under a flat roof or water after a storm: get matched with up to 3 licensed, insured roofers who find and fix leaks on Oak Ridge homes. Free, with no obligation.
intro: Leaks on Oak Ridge houses tend to come from the features that make them distinctive: chimneys set into small roofs, flat and low-slope sections that hold water, enclosed porches, and seams where decades of additions meet the original house. Shaded, wooded lots add leaves and moisture to the mix. This page explains where to look on wartime and postwar homes, what a roofer should do to trace water to its source, and how to tell when chasing leaks has stopped making sense.

sections.heading: Leak points on wartime and postwar houses
body: After the government began selling Oak Ridge houses in 1956, owners started changing them, and the National Register survey of the cemesto area lists porches that were screened, glassed in or fully enclosed. An enclosed porch usually keeps its original roof, and the joint where that roof meets the house wall is a common source of drips that now land inside a finished room.

In Woodland and Scarboro, look closely at any house where a gable roof was later framed over an original flat one. The transition at the eaves, and whatever was left of the old roof underneath, can trap water or hide where it is coming from. On the hipped Model 20 duplexes, two chimneys sit right at the crest, so their flashing takes water from both slopes.

sections.heading: Shade, leaves and steady moisture
body: A roof under tall trees on a ridge lot dries slowly. Leaves pack into valleys and gutters, water backs up under the first course of shingles, and shaded slopes grow moss that lifts shingle edges. With Knoxville-area relative humidity averaging about 72 percent, attic condensation can also pass for a leak, especially in a house with added insulation and little ventilation.
Clearing valleys and gutters each fall, and trimming limbs back from the roof, prevents many of these leaks before they start.

sections.heading: Tracing the water to its source
body: On a sloped roof, a roofer should start in the attic, follow stains along the rafters and deck, and photograph the entry point. On a flat roof, water can travel under the membrane before it drips, so expect probing around seams, edges and penetrations, and possibly a water test. HomeAdvisor's 2026 national range for leak repair is about $360 to $1,550.
If the trail leads to a wall with siding over original cemesto, ask how the roofer will reach the flashing without breaking the panels.

sections.heading: When to stop patching
body: Flat roofs have shorter lives than shingles. InterNACHI estimates about 20 years for modified bitumen, 15 to 25 for EPDM and 7 to 20 for TPO. If a low-slope roof in that age range leaks in a new place every season, or the deck under it has gone soft, the money is usually better spent on a new membrane than on more patches.

checklist: Write down which rooms leak and whether it happens in every rain or only in storms
Ask whether the leak is at a porch, addition or chimney joint
For a flat roof, ask how the roofer will find where water enters the membrane
Ask whether attic ventilation or condensation could be part of the problem
Confirm how siding over cemesto walls will be handled if flashing must be reached
Get photos of the source and the finished repair

faqs.q: Why does my enclosed porch in Oak Ridge leak when the rest of the house doesn't?
faqs.a: A porch roof can be lower in pitch than the main roof, and when a porch is closed in, the room beneath it shows every drip that an open porch used to hide. Water usually gets in where the porch roof meets the house wall. Ask the roofer to check the flashing there and whether the porch roof's slope suits the material on it.

faqs.q: Is it safe for a roofer to remove siding on my cemesto house to fix a leak?
faqs.a: It depends on what is under the siding. The original cemesto panels are faced with asbestos cement, and the EPA says material that will be disturbed should be sampled by a trained, accredited professional first. Many leaks can be reached without breaking the panels, so ask the roofer to explain the approach before any siding comes off.

faqs.q: How fast can a roofer look at a leak in Oak Ridge?
faqs.a: Roofers you are matched with usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours. If water is coming in now, mention it on the form, set out buckets, and move anything valuable away from the drip. Don't climb onto a wet or mossy roof; a roofer can tarp it until the permanent repair is done.
